en: The Apadāna of the Elder Nun Puṇṇikā, from the Khattiyā Chapter (8) of the Therīapadāna.
“Of the Blessed One Vipassī,
of Sikhin and Vessabhu,
and of the Sage Kakusandha— ”
Under the dispensation of the Buddha Koṇāgamana and others, and under that of the Buddha Kassapa,
having gone forth into homelessness;
A bhikkhunī endowed with virtue,
prudent, with senses restrained,
learned, and a bearer of the Dhamma—
One who questions on the established Dhamma, one who has mastered the teachings,
one who listens, and one who attends respectfully.
Descending here into the midst of people,
I was one in the teaching of the Jina;
by means of that great learning, I—
I despised those who were virtuous.
Now, in my final existence,
in Sāvatthī, the most excellent city;
Born in the house of Anāthapiṇḍika as the daughter of a water-carrier slave,
I went out to fetch water.
I saw a physician being given [an offering];
seeing him standing in the midst of the water, cold with chill, I spoke these words.
“O Sītā, I was a water-carrier;
I always drew water,
terrified by the fear of my masters’ punishment.”
"Abiding in fear of faults in speech,
of whom are you afraid, O brahmin,
that you always descend into the water?"
"With your limbs trembling,
you experience intense cold.
"Truly, lady, you know me well!"
Puṇṇikā, you ask about one who performs wholesome karma and obstructs the evil that has been done.
Whether it be an elder or a youth,
whoever commits an evil deed—
even he [is purified] by the sprinkling of water.
One is liberated from evil deeds.
To him who was crossing over,
I proclaimed the word endowed with the meaning of the Dhamma.

Having heard that, he was moved with spiritual urgency; having gone forth, he became an arahant. Filling up the number of less than a hundred, they were all liberated from the bonds of Māra. Thus it was said. How was it? At one time, the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. At that time, there were ninety-nine bhikkhus dwelling in the Kosalā country who had not yet attained arahantship. Then the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus!”—“Venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this: “Bhikkhus, if even ninety-nine bhikkhus dwelling in the Kosalā country have not yet attained arahantship, what can be said of the rest? Therefore, bhikkhus, you should train yourselves thus: ‘We will strive for the attainment of the as-yet-unattained, for the achievement of the as-yet-unachieved, for the realization of the as-yet-unrealized. This is how it was said. And how was it said? At one time, the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Since I was born into the family of a slave,
they gave me the name Puṇṇā and made me a free woman.
Having obtained the merchant’s permission,
I went forth into the homeless life;
and in no long time, I—
I attained arahantship;
I am a master of the supernormal powers and possess the divine ear-element.
O Great Sage, I have mastery over the knowledge of the minds of others;
I know my former births.
The divine eye has been purified;
all taints are utterly exhausted;
there is now no further becoming.
In the meanings, the phenomena, the definitions,
and likewise in inspired eloquence,
my knowledge is stainless and pure.
Through the power of the Best of Buddhas,
she possesses great wisdom through meditation and is learned through her hearing of the teachings.
One born of a low family does not destroy their karma through pride;
for my defilements have been burnt away.
I dwell free from taints.
Welcome indeed has come to me!
... [and so on] ... the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
The four analytical knowledges (paṭisambhidā) have been attained.
the Buddha's teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed did the bhikkhunī Puṇṇikā speak these verses.
The legend of the Elder Nun Puṇṇikā is the eighth.
